docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
This page is for server owners and staff. Each entry starts from what you see (a console line, a chat message, a door that does nothing), explains the cause and gives the fix. Chat messages are the default English texts; console lines are written by Door+ with the [DoorPlus] prefix.

Run the action from a command to see the reason

Some refusals are silent when they come from a trigger. Run /dp toggle <door> (or the same from the console) to get the message that explains why the door does not move.

docs.title: Door+ is disabled at startup
docs.text:
When Door+ cannot start, it disables itself. Depending on when the error happened, /dp is then an unknown command or answers Door+ is disabled. Details are in the server console. In both cases, search the console for the first Door+ error after Enabling DoorPlus.

Console line Cause Fix This copy of Door+ was not downloaded from BuiltByBit or Voxel Shop. ... The jar is not an original marketplace download Download the jar again from your purchases page. See Licence, verification and privacy The marketplace reports that this download of Door+ has no usage rights ... The marketplace refused the purchase See If Door+ was disabled by mistake The purchase of Door+ could not be verified for 7 days (marketplace unreachable) ... The server could not reach the marketplace for 7 days Allow outgoing HTTPS to the marketplace, then restart Cannot load config.yml or the language files; disabling Door+ config.yml is not valid YAML (wrong indentation, a tab, a missing quote), or the plugins/DoorPlus/lang/ folder cannot be written Fix the line named in the error below that message, or rename config.yml so that Door+ creates a fresh copy, then restart Cannot open the database (sqlite): Database schema version <n> is newer than the supported version 2; update Door+ or restore a backup; disabling Door+ The database was written by a newer Door+ version (you downgraded the plugin) Install the newer Door+ again, or restore a backup of the database made before the update Cannot open the database (mysql): Cannot open the mysql database: <details>; disabling Door+ (or mariadb) Door+ cannot connect to the MySQL/MariaDB server Check storage.mysql.host, port, database, username and password; check that the database exists, the user has rights on it and the server is reachable from the Minecraft host Cannot open the database (sqlite): Cannot back up the SQLite database before migrating; disabling Door+ Before updating the database format Door+ copies doorplus.db to doorplus.db.bak-v<version>, and the copy failed Free disk space and check that the server can write to plugins/DoorPlus/ Door+ failed to start; disabling Unexpected error Collect the information listed below and report it

Note

An invalid value in config.yml (for example a number out of range) does not stop Door+: it is logged and replaced by its default. Only a config.yml that cannot be read at all stops the start-up. A broken language file does not stop Door+ either: the console shows Missing language key '<key>' in lang/<language>.yml; using the bundled text and the original English or Italian text is used. Changes to the storage section need a restart; /dp admin reload only logs Changes to the 'storage' section require a server restart.

If Door+ starts but then disables itself after a few seconds, read the purchase verification messages in Licence, verification and privacy.

docs.title: A door does not move
docs.text:
Find the message you see in the table. Messages marked "action bar" appear above the hotbar instead of in chat.

Message Cause Fix Door movements are paused by an administrator. An admin ran /dp admin pause Run /dp admin pause again to resume <door> is locked. (action bar) The door is locked; a lock blocks every trigger, command and the API /dp unlock <door> You cannot use <door>. (action bar) The player has no access: privacy, access list, key or trigger access mode See Players cannot use a door <door> cannot move: the block at <x>, <y>, <z> cannot be animated. A block of the door is not allowed in doors: in blocks.blacklist, missing from a non-empty blocks.whitelist, or a block with data (chest, sign, ...) Remove or replace that block, or change the block lists <door> cannot move: something is in the way at <x>, <y>, <z>. A block, or another door, is in the destination or on the path the door travels (movement.check-swept-volume) Clear that block. Blocks in blocks.replaceable (water, grass, snow, ...) and blocks.passable (barrier, light, structure void) never block a door <door> cannot move beyond the height limits of the world. The destination is above the build limit or below the world bottom Change the direction or the blocks to move (/dp set <door> direction, blocks-to-move) <door> cannot move here: denied by <hook>. A protection plugin forbids doors in the destination See WorldGuard denies an action The world of <door> is not loaded. (commands only) The door's world is not loaded Load the world Door not found. (commands only) The name is wrong, or you have no role on that door Use #<id> or <owner>:<name>; see Players cannot edit a door <door> could not move because of an error. Details are in the server console. Unexpected error Report it with the console error, see below

Silent cases: the door does not move and no message is shown when:

  • the door is already in the requested state (an "Open" trigger on an open door);
  • the door is already moving;
  • the door cooldown has not expired (movement.toggle-cooldown-ticks, 0 by default);
  • another plugin cancelled the movement through the API.

docs.title: A trigger does nothing
docs.text:
1. Run /dp trigger inspect and click the source: Door+ lists the triggers linked to it, with action and state. No triggers you can see are linked to this source. means the trigger is missing or belongs to another door.
  2. Run /dp trigger list <door> and check that the trigger is enabled. Enable it with /dp trigger set <trigger id> enabled true.
  3. Check the cases below.
Symptom Cause Fix A redstone trigger never works Redstone triggers are off on the server (triggers.redstone.enabled: false), or the door does not allow redstone. New doors do not allow it by default (defaults.allow-redstone: false) /dp set <door> redstone true; ask an admin to set triggers.redstone.enabled: true A player clicks and nothing happens, no message The player was holding an item while sneaking (that click is ignored on purpose), or another plugin denied the click (for example a protection plugin in that area) Click with an empty hand or without sneaking; allow block interaction in that area The action bar shows You cannot use <door>. The player has no access Change the door privacy, or the trigger access mode with /dp trigger set <trigger id> access <mode> The trigger works only every few clicks The trigger cooldown (triggers.default-cooldown-ticks, 10 ticks by default) or the door is still moving Wait for the movement to end, or lower the cooldown with /dp trigger set <trigger id> cooldown <ticks> An "Open" (or "Close") trigger does nothing The door is already open (or closed) Use the "Toggle" action A custom block, furniture or NPC trigger stopped working The integration is missing or off; the console shows <Plugin>: not installed; ... or <Plugin>: disabled in config (integrations.<name>); ... Install the plugin or set integrations.<name>: true, then restart The trigger disappeared Its source (entity, custom block, furniture, NPC) was removed. The door owner sees The source of trigger #<id> (<type>) of <door> at <x> <y> <z> disappeared: the trigger was removed. Link the trigger again

See Triggers for actions, access modes and every trigger setting.

docs.title: Players cannot open or edit doors
Players cannot use a door
docs.text:
The action bar shows You cannot use <door>.

  1. Check the privacy with /dp info <door>. New doors are Private by default: only the owner and the admins can use them.
  2. To let everyone use it: /dp privacy <door> public.
  3. To let only some players use it: /dp privacy <door> restricted, then add them with /dp access add <door> player <name> (or group <group>, permission <node>).
  4. If the door has a key with mode Key required, the player must also hold the key.
  5. If the player uses a trigger, the trigger access mode can override the privacy (/dp trigger list <door>).

See Privacy and roles and Keys.

docs.title: Players cannot edit a door
docs.text:
Message Cause Fix Requires role <role> on this door. (menu) The button needs a higher role: Admin to change settings and triggers, Owner to change privacy, access, transfer or delete Ask the owner to give the player the Admin role You need to be an admin of that door. (command) Same, from a command Same Door not found. The player has no role on the door, so it is hidden from them Add the player to the access list You do not have permission to do this. The player lacks a command permission. By default every player has them through doorplus.user Check that your permission plugin does not remove doorplus.user or doorplus.command.*

To take over a door whose owner is gone, an admin can run /dp admin claim <door>. See Permissions.

docs.title: Players cannot create doors
docs.text:
Message Cause Fix You do not have permission to do this. Missing doorplus.create.<type>; by default only operators have it Give doorplus.create.<type> or doorplus.create.* You already own the maximum number of doors (<limit>). limits.doors-per-player (10 by default) Raise the limit, or give doorplus.limit.doors.<n> The region has more than <limit> blocks, the most you can use for a door. limits.max-door-blocks (500 by default) Raise the limit, or give doorplus.limit.size.<n> Doors cannot be created in the world <world>. The world is in worlds.disabled Remove it from the list Doors of type <type> are disabled on this server. types.<type>.enabled: false Set it to true You cannot create a door here (denied by <hook>). A protection plugin denies the area See WorldGuard denies an action You need a free inventory slot for the creation stick. Full inventory Free one slot

See Creating a door and Limits.

docs.title: Animation invisible, choppy or flickering
docs.text:
Symptom Cause Fix The door jumps to its new position without animation No player was within animation.viewer-range (64 blocks); or the door has more blocks than animation.max-animated-blocks (1500); or the server was already animating animation.max-global-animated-blocks (10000); or a chunk of the door had to be loaded Expected behaviour. Raise these values if you need it The moving blocks disappear when seen from far away The animation entities have a limited view range Raise animation.display.view-range (1.0 by default) Moving blocks look darker or flicker Light changes while blocks move Keep animation.display.fixed-brightness: true Console: animation.engine is falling_block but that engine is unavailable; using block_display The falling_block engine does not work on this server version Use animation.engine: block_display (the default) Console: Shulker colliders cannot be spawned (blocked by another plugin?); the shulker collision mode falls back to push Another plugin prevents spawning shulkers Allow Door+ to spawn entities, or use another collision mode The animation is too fast or too slow Speed settings Change the door speed (/dp set <door> speed <multiplier>) or speed.* in the config

See Movement and animation.

docs.title: Leftover animation entities
docs.text:
Animation entities are never saved with the world, and Door+ removes leftovers by itself: at start-up (the console shows Removed <n> orphan animation entities) and every time a chunk with leftovers loads.

If you still see frozen floating blocks after a crash:

  1. Stand near them so that their chunks are loaded.
  2. Run /dp admin cleanup. The reply is Removed <count> orphan entities.

Missing door blocks after a crash are restored from the journal at the next start (Journal: recovered <n> of <total> interrupted door movements). If the console shows Journal row of door #<id> kept: its world is not loaded, load that world and restart the server: the movement is completed then.

docs.title: WorldGuard denies an action
docs.text:
Message Cause Fix You cannot create a door here (denied by WorldGuard). The player cannot build in a region the door touches (closed or open position), or a region has the flag doorplus-create set to deny Add the player as a member of the region, or set doorplus-create to allow. Players with doorplus.admin.bypass.protection or WorldGuard bypass skip this check <door> cannot move here: denied by WorldGuard. A region where the door would move has doorplus-toggle set to deny. This applies to everyone, including admins Remove the flag, or set it to allow The protection WorldGuard does not allow you to link this source. The player cannot build where the trigger source is Add the player to that region, or link the source as someone who can build there

See WorldGuard.

docs.title: Placeholders are empty
docs.text:
1. Check the console at start-up. You must see PlaceholderAPI <version>: active (expansion doorplus). If you see PlaceholderAPI: not installed; Door+ placeholders unavailable or disabled in config, install PlaceholderAPI or set integrations.placeholderapi: true, then restart. Door+ registers its own expansion: do not download one from the eCloud.
  2. Check the spelling: every placeholder starts with %doorplus_. An unknown placeholder returns an empty text.
  3. Door names in placeholders work like in commands: a plain name means a door of the player viewing it. For other doors use #<id> or <owner>:<name>.
  4. Player placeholders, and nearest / looking placeholders, need an online player. nearest only finds doors within placeholders.nearest-radius (16 blocks) and looking within placeholders.looking-distance (10 blocks).
  5. The text shown for unknown values is the placeholder.unknown key of the language file, empty by default.

See Placeholders.

docs.title: Collecting information for a bug report
docs.text:
Send all of the following on the support Discord:

  1. Run /dp admin version and copy every line: plugin, API and server versions, storage, animation engine, integrations, hooks and providers, numbers of doors, triggers and groups.
  2. If a specific door misbehaves, run /dp admin debug <door>. The reply is State of <door> #<id> written to the console.; copy the Debug dump of ... block from the console.
  3. Turn on detailed logs: set debug: true in config.yml and run /dp admin reload. Door+ then writes extra lines starting with [debug] (triggers linked and removed, auto-close results, creation problems). Reproduce the problem, then set debug: false again.
  4. Attach logs/latest.log from the moment the server started. Include full error stack traces, unchanged: Door+ is obfuscated, and the author can read the scrambled names.
  5. Describe the exact steps to reproduce the problem and what you expected.
  6. If relevant, attach config.yml. Remove storage.mysql.password first.

docs.title: Integrations
docs.text:
This page lists the plugins Door+ works with, what each one adds, and how to check which integrations are active on your server. It is for server administrators.

All integrations are optional. Door+ works on its own; when one of these plugins is installed, Door+ connects to it automatically at startup. You do not need to download any add-on.

docs.title: Supported plugins
docs.text:
Plugin What it adds Page LuckPerms Access entries for LuckPerms groups, with group lists in menus and tab completion LuckPerms WorldGuard Build checks when creating doors and linking triggers, the flags doorplus-create and doorplus-toggle, region access for doors WorldGuard PlaceholderAPI The %doorplus_...% placeholders PlaceholderAPI ItemsAdder Custom blocks and furniture as triggers, custom items as keys Custom blocks and furniture Nexo Custom blocks and furniture as triggers, custom items as keys Custom blocks and furniture Oraxen Custom blocks and furniture as triggers, custom items as keys Custom blocks and furniture CraftEngine Custom blocks and furniture as triggers, custom items as keys Custom blocks and furniture Citizens NPCs as triggers NPCs FancyNpcs NPCs as triggers NPCs

Door+ 1.0.0 was built against these versions of the plugin APIs: LuckPerms 5.5, WorldGuard 7.0.17 (WorldEdit 7.3.18), PlaceholderAPI 2.12.3, ItemsAdder 4.0.17, Nexo 1.30.2, Oraxen 1.220.1, CraftEngine 26.10, Citizens 2.0.44, FancyNpcs 2.9.2. LuckPerms, WorldGuard (with FastAsyncWorldEdit), PlaceholderAPI, ItemsAdder and FancyNpcs were also tested on a live Paper 1.21.8 server.

Other plugins can add their own protection checks, custom block sources and NPC sources through the Door+ API: see Extension points.

docs.title: Detection at startup
docs.text:
When Door+ starts, it checks each plugin in the table. For each one it writes one line in the console:

Console line Meaning <Plugin> <version>: active (...) The integration works. The brackets say what was enabled, e.g. WorldGuard 7.0.17: active (protection hook, region access, flags doorplus-create, doorplus-toggle). <Plugin>: not installed; ... unavailable The plugin is missing or not enabled. <Plugin>: disabled in config (integrations.<name>); ... off You switched the integration off in config.yml. <Plugin>: hook failed, integration disabled The plugin is installed but Door+ could not connect to it (usually an incompatible version). The console shows the error below this line.

ItemsAdder, Nexo, Oraxen and CraftEngine load their content after the server starts. Until then the line ends with waiting for data, and a second line <name> data loaded (e.g. itemsadder data loaded) appears when the content is ready.

Note

Door+ looks for the plugins only when it starts. If you install, remove or update one of these plugins, restart the server. /dp admin reload does not connect or disconnect integrations.

docs.title: Switching an integration off
docs.text:
Every integration has a switch in config.yml. Set it to false to keep Door+ away from a plugin even when that plugin is installed:

integrations:                  # false = do not hook even if the plugin is installed
  luckperms: true
  placeholderapi: true
  worldguard: true
  itemsadder: true
  nexo: true
  oraxen: true
  craftengine: true
  citizens: true
  fancynpcs: true

Restart the server after changing a switch. See Configuration.

docs.title: Seeing the active integrations
docs.text:
Run /dp admin version (permission doorplus.admin.version). Two lines matter here:

Line Shows Integrations: The integrations that started, by their config.yml name, e.g. luckperms, worldguard, itemsadder, placeholderapi, or none. Hooks and providers: What is plugged into Door+ right now: protection:<name> (protection checks such as protection:WorldGuard), content:<name> (custom block plugins such as content:itemsadder), npc:<name> (NPC plugins such as npc:fancynpcs), or none. Hooks added by other plugins through the API appear here too.

docs.title: Custom blocks and furniture
docs.text:
This page explains how to use the custom blocks, furniture and items of ItemsAdder, Nexo, Oraxen and CraftEngine with Door+. It is for server owners and door owners on servers with one of these plugins.

With one of these plugins installed, Door+ adds:

Feature Trigger type Page A placed custom block opens the door when right-clicked Custom block Triggers A placed furniture opens the door when right-clicked Furniture Triggers A custom item works as the door key — Keys

No configuration is needed. Each plugin can be switched off with integrations.itemsadder, integrations.nexo, integrations.oraxen or integrations.craftengine in config.yml (see Integrations).

docs.title: Wait until the content is loaded
docs.text:
These plugins load their blocks and items a little after the server starts. Door+ recognises custom content only after that. The console shows <plugin> data loaded, e.g. itemsadder data loaded.

Warning

If you link a custom block before its plugin has loaded, Door+ sees an ordinary block and creates a normal Block trigger. If you click furniture too early you see This object is not recognised yet. Try again in a moment. Wait for the console line, then link again.

docs.title: Linking a custom block
docs.text:
You need the Admin role on the door and the permissions doorplus.trigger.block and doorplus.trigger.custom_block (every player has them by default through doorplus.user).

MenuCommand
  1. Open the door menu and click Triggers.
  2. Click Add trigger, then Block.
  3. Click the custom block in the world.
  1. Run /dp trigger add <door> block [action], e.g. /dp trigger add castle_gate block toggle.
  2. Click the custom block in the world.

You see Linked Custom block trigger #<id> to <door>. If Door+ says Block instead of Custom block, the plugin had not loaded yet (see above).

docs.title: Linking furniture
docs.text:
You need the Admin role on the door and the permissions doorplus.trigger.entity and doorplus.trigger.furniture (every player has them by default).

MenuCommand
  1. Open the door menu and click Triggers.
  2. Click Add trigger, then Entity.
  3. Click the furniture in the world.
  1. Run /dp trigger add <door> entity [action], e.g. /dp trigger add castle_gate entity open.
  2. Click the furniture in the world.

You see Linked Furniture trigger #<id> to <door>.

ItemsAdder complex furniture

Complex (multi-entity) furniture works like simple furniture. Door+ stores the id of its custom entity, which can differ from the id of the furniture item: /dp trigger inspect shows the stored id.

Oraxen shaped blocks

Custom stairs, slabs, doors and trapdoors of Oraxen work as custom blocks. A two-block door counts only on the half you linked.

docs.title: How these triggers behave
docs.text:
• A trigger fires when a player right-clicks the custom block or furniture.
  • Available actions: Toggle, Open, Close, and Go to stop for platforms. Follow state is not available, because a custom block has no on/off state.
  • The player must be allowed to use the door, as for any trigger (see Triggers).
  • By default the click is consumed: the plugin's own action for that block or furniture (for example sitting on a chair) does not happen. To let it happen as well, run /dp trigger set <trigger id> cancel-vanilla false.

docs.title: Custom item ids
docs.text:
Door+ stores the id each plugin gives to its content:

Plugin Id format Example ItemsAdder namespace:id castle:gate_lever Nexo item id gate_lever Oraxen item id gate_lever CraftEngine namespace:id castle:gate_lever

The provider column of the trigger menu and of /dp trigger list shows the plugin (itemsadder, nexo, oraxen, craftengine).

docs.title: Custom items as keys
docs.text:
Any custom item from these plugins can be the key of a door. All items with the same custom id open the door, so you can sell or craft keys with your item plugin.

MenuCommand
  1. Hold the custom item in your main hand.
  2. Open the door menu, click Key, then Use the custom item in hand.
  3. Set the Mode to Key as alternative or Key required.
  1. Hold the custom item in your main hand.
  2. Run /dp key custom <door>. You see The custom item in your hand is now the key of <door>.
  3. Run /dp key mode <door> alternative or /dp key mode <door> required.

The key is saved as CUSTOM:<plugin>:<id>, e.g. CUSTOM:itemsadder:castle:gate_key. Ids are compared without regard to upper and lower case. If the item in your hand is not a custom item, you see The item in your hand is not a custom item recognised by Door+.

Modes, consumption and where the key must be held are explained in Keys.

docs.title: When the source or item disappears
docs.text: What happens Result Someone breaks the linked custom block or furniture The trigger is removed. If the door owner is online (and is not the one who broke it), they get The source of trigger #<id> (<type>) of <door> at x y z disappeared: the trigger was removed. The door has Protect blocks on Only players with the Admin role (or a bypass permission) can break its trigger sources. Others see This object is a protected trigger source. A different custom block now stands where the linked one was The trigger is removed the next time someone clicks it. The plugin replaces the furniture with a new copy of the same item at the same block The trigger moves to the new copy automatically the first time someone clicks it. The block or furniture vanishes without being broken (removed by a command, a world edit, or the item is deleted from the plugin's configuration) The trigger stays in the list but no longer fires. Remove it from the trigger menu or with /dp trigger remove <trigger id>. The custom content plugin is uninstalled Its triggers stay saved but do nothing. They work again if you reinstall the plugin. The key item is deleted from the plugin, or the plugin is uninstalled No item matches the key any more. With Key required, only the owner, Admins and players with doorplus.admin.bypass.use can use the door. Set a new key or remove it with /dp key remove <door>.

docs.title: LuckPerms
docs.text: This page explains what Door+ does with LuckPerms: giving a whole permission group access to a door. It is for server administrators and door owners.

docs.title: What LuckPerms adds
docs.text:
With LuckPerms installed you can add group access entries to a door: every member of the LuckPerms group gets the role you choose (User or Admin). Without LuckPerms you can still add player entries and permission entries, but not group entries.

With LuckPerms Without LuckPerms Add a group entry Yes. Menus and tab completion list the groups LuckPerms has loaded. No: the command answers Group entries require LuckPerms. and the menu button shows Requires LuckPerms. Group entries already saved Checked normally Still checked through the group.<name> permission (usually nobody has it)

The same group entries work in the access list of a trigger (see Triggers).

docs.title: Giving a group access to a door
docs.text:
You need the Owner role on the door (or the bypass permissions of an operator) and the permission doorplus.access.group, which every player has by default through doorplus.user.

MenuCommand
  1. Open the door menu and click Access list.
  2. Click Add LuckPerms group. The menu Choose a LuckPerms group opens.
  3. Click the group.
  4. Choose the role (User or Admin).
/dp access add <door> group <group> [user|admin]

Example: /dp access add castle_gate group guards admin. Without a role the entry gets User. To remove it: /dp access remove castle_gate group guards.

Group names are stored in lower case and can contain letters, digits, _, . and - (at most 64 characters).

Remember that only Restricted doors let access entries with the User role in. Admin entries can use the door with any privacy. See Privacy and roles.

docs.title: How membership is checked
docs.text:
For a player who is online, Door+ checks the permission group.<name>, which LuckPerms gives to every member of a group, including members through inheritance. There is no cache on the Door+ side: when you add a player to a group or remove them, the change applies to doors immediately.

If you delete a group in LuckPerms, the entry stays on the door and the access list shows it in red with This LuckPerms group no longer exists. Remove it with shift + right click in the menu or with /dp access remove.

Note

Checks for players who are offline (only used by other plugins through the Door+ API) ask LuckPerms for the player's groups and permissions. Without LuckPerms, offline checks only see player entries.

docs.title: Limits per group
docs.text:
Door+ limits can be raised with permission nodes (doorplus.limit.doors.<n>, doorplus.limit.size.<n>, doorplus.limit.triggers.<n>). With LuckPerms you give them to a group like any other permission:

/lp group vip permission set doorplus.limit.doors.25 true

The highest number a player has wins. See Limits and Permissions.

docs.title: NPCs
docs.text:
This page explains how to make a Citizens or FancyNpcs NPC open a door when a player right-clicks it. It is for server owners and door owners on servers with one of these plugins.

With Citizens or FancyNpcs installed, an NPC can be a trigger of type NPC: a gatekeeper that opens the castle gate, a lift operator that sends a platform to a stop, and so on. No configuration is needed. Each plugin can be switched off with integrations.citizens or integrations.fancynpcs in config.yml (see Integrations).

docs.title: Linking an NPC
docs.text:
You need the Admin role on the door and the permissions doorplus.trigger.entity and doorplus.trigger.npc (every player has them by default through doorplus.user).

MenuCommand
  1. Open the door menu and click Triggers.
  2. Click Add trigger, then Entity.
  3. Right-click the NPC.
  1. Run /dp trigger add <door> entity [action], e.g. /dp trigger add castle_gate entity toggle.
  2. Right-click the NPC.

You see Linked NPC trigger #<id> to <door>. You have triggers.selection-timeout-seconds seconds (default 30) to click; type /dp cancel to stop.

The usual trigger rules apply when linking (see Triggers):

  • The NPC must be in the same world as the door.
  • It must be within limits.max-trigger-distance blocks of the door (default 64), measured where the NPC stands when you link it.
  • With WorldGuard, you must be allowed to build where the NPC stands (see WorldGuard).

If Door+ answers This object is not recognised yet. Try again in a moment., neither Citizens nor FancyNpcs reported the clicked NPC as one of theirs. Try again; if the message repeats, check the NPC in its own plugin.

docs.title: How NPC triggers behave
docs.text:
• The trigger fires when a player right-clicks the NPC. Left clicks do nothing.
  • Available actions: Toggle, Open, Close, and Go to stop for platforms. Follow state is not available.
  • The player must be allowed to use the door, as for any trigger. To let everyone use the door through the NPC while the door itself stays private, change the access of the trigger (see Triggers).
  • By default the NPC's own click actions (Citizens commands, FancyNpcs actions) still run. To stop them when the click is used by Door+, run /dp trigger set <trigger id> cancel-vanilla true.
  • The trigger is tied to the NPC itself, not to a position: you can move or teleport the NPC and the trigger keeps working.

Door+ identifies NPCs by an id that survives restarts: the NPC's UUID for Citizens, the NPC id from the save file for FancyNpcs.

To see which triggers an NPC has, run /dp trigger inspect and right-click the NPC.

docs.title: When the NPC is deleted
docs.text:
What happens Result The NPC is deleted in Citizens or FancyNpcs Its triggers are removed. If the door owner is online, they get The source of trigger #<id> (NPC) of <door> at x y z disappeared: the trigger was removed. The coordinates are where the NPC was when it was linked. The server stops, or Citizens unloads its NPCs while shutting down Nothing: the triggers stay. The NPC plugin is uninstalled The triggers stay saved but do nothing. They work again if you reinstall the plugin and the NPC still exists.

A trigger can always be removed by hand from the trigger menu or with /dp trigger remove <trigger id>.

docs.title: PlaceholderAPI
docs.text: This page explains how to use the Door+ placeholders in other plugins through PlaceholderAPI. It is for server owners who build scoreboards, holograms, tab lists and menus.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
1. Install PlaceholderAPI.
  2. Restart the server.

That is all. The Door+ expansion is built into the plugin: you do not need /papi ecloud download. At startup the console shows:

PlaceholderAPI <version>: active (expansion doorplus)

The expansion is called doorplus and stays registered after /papi reload.

To test a placeholder in game, use PlaceholderAPI's parse command:

/papi parse me %doorplus_version%

The full list of placeholders, with examples, is on the Placeholders page.

To keep Door+ away from PlaceholderAPI, set integrations.placeholderapi: false in config.yml and restart (see Integrations).

docs.title: Choosing the right placeholder
docs.text:
You want to show Use The state of one specific door, to everyone %doorplus_door_<id>_<field>%, e.g. %doorplus_door_12_state_display% Information about the door a player is standing next to %doorplus_nearest_<field>% Information about the door a player is looking at %doorplus_looking_<field>% Statistics about the player %doorplus_player_<field>% Statistics about the server %doorplus_total%, %doorplus_moving%, ...

Holograms and shared scoreboards

Refer to a door by its id (12 or #12) or by owner:name. A bare door name only finds doors owned by the player viewing the line, so other players would see an empty value. Get the id with /dp info <door>.

docs.title: Example: scoreboard
docs.text:
Lines for a scoreboard plugin that shows information about the door next to the player:

Door: %doorplus_nearest_name%
State: %doorplus_nearest_state_display%
Owner: %doorplus_nearest_owner%
Can use: %doorplus_nearest_can_use%
Your doors: %doorplus_player_owned%/%doorplus_player_limit%

When no door is within placeholders.nearest-radius blocks (default 16), the door lines show the unknown text, which is empty by default. Change placeholder.unknown in the language file if you prefer a dash or "none" (see Language files).

docs.title: Example: hologram above a gate
docs.text:
Lines for a hologram plugin, for the door with id 12:

%doorplus_door_12_name%
%doorplus_door_12_state_display%
Opened %doorplus_door_12_toggle_count% times
Last used by %doorplus_door_12_last_toggled_by%

For a group of doors (id 7):

West wing: %doorplus_group_7_open%/%doorplus_group_7_doors% doors open

docs.title: Yes/no values
docs.text: Placeholders such as is_open, is_locked or can_use show true or false. These texts come from the keys placeholder.true and placeholder.false of the language file, so you can change them, e.g. to Yes / No. Placeholder values are plain text: MiniMessage colour tags in these keys are removed.

docs.title: WorldGuard
docs.text:
This page explains how Door+ respects WorldGuard regions, the two Door+ flags, and region access for doors. It is for server administrators who protect their worlds with WorldGuard.

With WorldGuard installed, Door+ adds five things:

Feature Applies to Build check on creation Creating and redefining doors Flag doorplus-create Creating and redefining doors Flag doorplus-toggle Every door movement Build check on trigger linking Linking a trigger source Region access Who can use a door

docs.title: Build check when creating a door
docs.text:
To create a door, or to redefine its region, a player must be allowed to build in every WorldGuard region that touches:

  • the door itself (its closed position), and
  • the space the door occupies when it is open.

If one region refuses, the creation stops with You cannot create a door here (denied by WorldGuard).

This uses WorldGuard's normal build rules: region members and owners can build, the build flag applies, and so do global region settings.

docs.title: Flag doorplus-create
docs.text:
A state flag, default allow. Set it to deny to stop everyone, members and owners included, from creating doors in a region:

/rg flag castle doorplus-create deny

The check covers the same space as the build check above. To remove the flag again:

/rg flag castle doorplus-create

docs.title: Flag doorplus-toggle
docs.text:
A state flag, default allow. Set it to deny to stop doors from moving into a region:

/rg flag spawn doorplus-toggle deny

Door+ checks the position the door is moving to. A door whose open position touches the region cannot open; a door whose closed position touches the region cannot close. Windmills, flags and clocks cannot be started if their blocks touch the region.

The flag applies to every movement, whoever or whatever starts it (players, triggers, redstone, commands, the console, auto-close), and there is no bypass. A refused movement shows <door> cannot move here: denied by WorldGuard. to the player who started it.

docs.title: Build check when linking a trigger
docs.text: To link a trigger, a player must be allowed to build at the position of the source (the button, block, entity, furniture or NPC). Otherwise the link is refused with The protection WorldGuard does not allow you to link this source. See Triggers.

docs.title: Bypass
docs.text:
Who Skips Players with WorldGuard's region bypass in that world The build checks and doorplus-create Players with doorplus.admin.bypass.protection (operators by default) The build checks and doorplus-create, for every protection plugin

Nothing bypasses doorplus-toggle.

docs.title: Region access
docs.text:
Region access lets the members of a WorldGuard region use a door without adding them one by one.

When region access is on for a door, every player who is a member or owner of a WorldGuard region containing the centre of the door (closed position) gets the User role on that door, unless they already have a higher role.

  • The door must be Restricted: like any User entry, region access does nothing on Private doors, and Public doors are open to everyone anyway.
  • Members of parent regions and WorldGuard groups count. The __global__ region does not.
  • Region owners get User, not Admin.
  • Only online players are checked.

To switch it on (you need the Admin role on the door):

MenuCommand
  1. Open the door menu.
  2. Click Region access. The lore shows WorldGuard region members: on.
/dp set <door> region-access true

Use false to switch it off.

New doors start with the value of defaults.region-access (default false).

If WorldGuard is not active, you can still switch the option on, but it has no effect: the command warns WorldGuard is not active: region access has no effect until it is installed. and the menu shows WorldGuard is not active on this server.

Warning

Region access works only on Restricted doors. When the door is Private, the region access button shows The door is PRIVATE: set it to RESTRICTED for region access to work., and switching region access on (or making such a door Private) by command shows <door> is PRIVATE: region members can open it only when it is RESTRICTED (/door privacy <door> restricted). See Privacy and roles.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
At startup the console shows which features are on, for example:

WorldGuard 7.0.17: active (protection hook, region access, flags doorplus-create, doorplus-toggle)
  • custom flags unavailable at the end of the line: the flags could not be registered. Door+ registers them while the server starts; if Door+ is loaded later by a plugin manager, WorldGuard no longer accepts new flags. Restart the server. The build checks and region access still work without the flags.
  • /rg flag says the flag does not exist: same cause, restart the server.
  • Setting integrations.worldguard: false turns off all the checks above and region access. The two flags are still registered when WorldGuard is installed, but have no effect.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text: This page lists every Door+ command with its exact syntax, the permission it needs, the role you need on the door, and examples. It is for players and staff who prefer commands to menus, and for administrators who run commands from the console.

docs.title: Basics
docs.text:
• The root command is /doorplus. The aliases /dp and /door do exactly the same thing. This page uses /dp.
  • Syntax: <required>, [optional], a|b means "type one of these".
  • Subcommands, options and values are not case-sensitive (/dp OPEN gate works).
  • In enum values you can type - or _ (owner-only and owner_only are the same).
  • Yes/no values accept true, on, yes or false, off, no.
  • /dp with no arguments opens the main menu if you have doorplus.command.menu. Otherwise (and in the console) it shows the help.
  • Tab completion only suggests the subcommands, doors, groups and values you are allowed to use.
  • Every command checks the permission first, then your role on the door. Roles are explained in Privacy and roles. For all permission nodes see Permissions.

Unknown or wrong commands

An unknown subcommand answers Unknown subcommand. Type /door help for the list. A command with wrong arguments answers Usage: followed by the correct syntax.

docs.title: Door references
docs.text:
Wherever a command asks for <door>, you can type the door in three ways:

Form Example Meaning #<id> #12 The door with that numeric ID. Always works. You see the ID in /dp list and /dp info. <name> castle_gate Your own door with that name. <owner>:<name> Steve:castle_gate A door owned by another player.

Rules:

  • Door names are 1 to 32 characters: letters, digits, _ and -. Names are not case-sensitive and are unique per owner, not per server.
  • You can only refer to doors on which you have a role (User, Admin or Owner), unless you have a bypass permission (doorplus.admin.bypass.use, .edit or .manage). Any other door answers Door not found., so nobody can discover doors they have no access to.
  • The console, and players with a bypass permission, can also use a bare <name> for another player's door if exactly one door on the server has that name. If several doors share the name, Door+ lists them, for example More doors are called gate: #5 (Mario), #9 (Luca). Use #id. Repeat the command with #id.
  • Tab completion shows your own doors first, then owner:name for doors shared with you. In the console it shows #id.

Group references (<group>) work the same way: #<id>, <name> (your own group) or <owner>:<name>. You can only use your own groups unless you have doorplus.admin.bypass.manage.

Groups in the console

The console has no "own" groups, so a bare group name does not work there. Use #<id> or <owner>:<name> (for example /dp group open #3). /dp group list in the console shows every group with its ID.

Trigger IDs (<trigger id>) are numbers, with or without #: 12 or #12. You see them in /dp trigger list.

docs.title: Quick reference
docs.text:
Command Permission Role on the door /dp help [page] none none /dp menu [<door>] doorplus.command.menu any role to open a door menu /dp create <type> [name] doorplus.create.<type> none /dp cancel none none /dp list [player] doorplus.command.list (+ doorplus.admin.list for another player) none /dp info <door> doorplus.command.info any role /dp toggle\|open\|close <door> [door...] doorplus.command.toggle decided by the door's access rules /dp goto <door> <stop> doorplus.command.toggle decided by the door's access rules /dp lock\|unlock <door> doorplus.command.manage Admin /dp rename <door> <name> doorplus.command.manage Admin /dp redefine <door> doorplus.command.manage Admin /dp set <door> <option> <value> doorplus.command.manage Admin /dp privacy <door> <private\|restricted\|public> doorplus.command.manage Owner /dp transfer <door> <player> doorplus.command.manage Owner /dp delete <door> [confirm] doorplus.command.manage Owner /dp tp <door> doorplus.command.teleport any role /dp access ... doorplus.command.manage Owner /dp trigger ... doorplus.command.manage (+ doorplus.trigger.<kind> for add) Admin (or owner of the group) /dp key ... doorplus.command.manage Admin /dp group toggle\|open\|close <group> doorplus.command.toggle owner of the group /dp group ... (other actions) doorplus.command.manage owner of the group; Admin on the door for add /dp admin ... one doorplus.admin.<action> node per action none

"Any role" means User, Admin or Owner, or a bypass permission. Players with doorplus.admin.bypass.edit act as Admin on every door, and players with doorplus.admin.bypass.manage act as Owner on every door. The console always acts as Owner.

docs.title: /dp help
docs.text:
/dp help [page]

Shows the commands you are allowed to use, 8 per page. page is a number from 1 to the last page. The last line tells you how to open the next page.

  • Permission: none.
  • Example: /dp help 2

docs.title: /dp menu
docs.text:
/dp menu [<door>]

Without a door, opens the main menu. With a door, opens the menu of that door. See Menus.

  • Permission: doorplus.command.menu.
  • Players only.
  • Example: /dp menu castle_gate

docs.title: /dp create
docs.text:
/dp create <type> [name]

Starts the guided creation of a new door. You receive the creation stick and follow the instructions in chat. See Creating a door.

  • type: one of big_door, drawbridge, portcullis, sliding_door, garage_door, split_door, folding_door, rolling_shutter, platform, revolving_door, windmill, flag, clock. Tab completion only shows the types you may create and that are enabled in types.<type>.enabled.
  • name (optional): 1 to 32 letters, digits, _ or -. If you leave it out, the creation asks for it.
  • Permission: doorplus.create.<type>, for example doorplus.create.big_door.
  • Players only.
  • Fails if the type is disabled in the configuration, if you reached your door limit (see Limits), if you already have a creation in progress, or if your inventory has no free slot for the creation stick.
  • Examples: /dp create big_door, /dp create sliding_door shop_door

docs.title: /dp cancel
docs.text:
/dp cancel

Cancels what you are doing right now, in this order: a door creation, then a trigger selection or inspection, then a chat input (for example a name you were asked to type). If nothing is in progress you see There is nothing to cancel.

  • Permission: none.
  • Players only.

docs.title: /dp list
docs.text:
/dp list [player]
  • Without a player: lists your own doors, then Doors shared with you (doors where you have a role).
  • With a player name: lists the doors owned by that player. Needs doorplus.admin.list as well (typing your own name does not).
  • In the console without a player: lists all doors of the server.
  • Each line shows #id, the door reference, the type, the state and the privacy.
  • Permission: doorplus.command.list.
  • Examples: /dp list, /dp list Steve

docs.title: /dp info
docs.text:
/dp info <door>

Shows the details of a door: type, state, owner, your role, location, size, number of blocks, direction, privacy, locked, redstone, protected blocks, region access, auto-close, speed, collisions, key mode, number of access entries, number of triggers and how many times it was operated.

  • Permission: doorplus.command.info.
  • Example: /dp info #12

docs.title: /dp toggle, /dp open, /dp close
docs.text:
/dp toggle <door> [door...]
/dp open <door> [door...]
/dp close <door> [door...]

Operates one or more doors. toggle opens a closed door and closes an open door; open and close only move the door if it is not already in that state. You can list several doors in one command.

  • Permission: doorplus.command.toggle.
  • Role: a player goes through the normal access check of the door (privacy, locked, key, cooldown), exactly as if they used it in the world. See Privacy and roles.
  • Console: the access check is skipped. The console sees Door ... is moving. for each door that starts moving.
  • Examples: /dp open castle_gate, /dp close gate_left gate_right, /dp toggle #12

docs.title: /dp goto
docs.text:
/dp goto <door> <stop>

Sends a platform to a stop. The first stop is 0, the last is the number of stops minus 1. Only works on doors of type platform; other doors answer ... is not a platform.

  • Permission: doorplus.command.toggle.
  • Role: same access check as /dp toggle. The console skips it.
  • Example: /dp goto elevator 2

docs.title: /dp tp
docs.text:
/dp tp <door>

Teleports you next to the door, facing it. If the door's world is not loaded you see The world ... of ... is not loaded.

  • Permission: doorplus.command.teleport (default: operators only).
  • Players only.
  • Example: /dp tp castle_gate

docs.title: /dp lock, /dp unlock
docs.text:
/dp lock <door>
/dp unlock <door>

Locks or unlocks a door. A locked door cannot be operated (see Privacy and roles).

  • Permission: doorplus.command.manage. Role: Admin.
  • Example: /dp lock vault_door

docs.title: /dp rename
docs.text:
/dp rename <door> <name>

Renames a door. The new name follows the name rules (1-32 letters, digits, _, -) and must not be used by another door of the same owner.

  • Permission: doorplus.command.manage. Role: Admin.
  • Example: /dp rename gate main_gate

docs.title: /dp redefine
docs.text:
/dp redefine <door>

Starts a guided session to select the region of the door again. See Editing a door.

  • Permission: doorplus.command.manage. Role: Admin.
  • Players only.
  • Example: /dp redefine castle_gate

docs.title: /dp set
docs.text:
/dp set <door> <option> <value>
/dp set <door> base-state

Changes one setting of a door. On success you see of set to .

  • Permission: doorplus.command.manage. Role: Admin.
Option Values Notes direction a direction allowed for this door: cw, ccw, up, down, north, east, south, west, none The door must be closed and still. Tab completion shows only the directions the door's type accepts. blocks-to-move 0 to limits.max-blocks-to-move 0 = the type's automatic value. Only for types that move by a number of blocks. The door must be closed and still. auto-close seconds, 0 to limits.max-auto-close-seconds 0 = no automatic closing. speed a decimal between limits.speed-multiplier.min and .max Speed multiplier, 1.0 = normal speed. collision default, or a mode listed in collision.allowed-modes: none, shulker, push default uses collision.default-mode. redstone true / false Whether redstone can operate the door. protect true / false Protects the door's blocks from being broken. region-access true / false Members of the WorldGuard region can use the door. If WorldGuard is not active you get a warning. See WorldGuard. base-state no value Makes the door's current position its closed state.

Some door types add their own options:

Option Door type mode split_door visible-rows rolling_shutter stops platform quarter-turns revolving_door degrees-per-second windmill time-source clock

Values and meaning of these options are explained on each type's page under Door types. Tab completion suggests valid values. An option the door does not have answers Unknown option ... for this door.

Examples:

/dp set castle_gate auto-close 10
/dp set castle_gate speed 1.5
/dp set castle_gate collision push
/dp set shop_door redstone true
/dp set lift stops 0,5,12
/dp set castle_gate base-state

docs.title: /dp privacy
docs.text:
/dp privacy <door> <private|restricted|public>

Sets who can use the door: private (owner and admins), restricted (owner, admins and every access entry), public (everyone).

  • Permission: doorplus.command.manage. Role: Owner.
  • Example: /dp privacy castle_gate restricted

docs.title: /dp transfer
docs.text:
/dp transfer <door> <player>

Gives the door to another player, who becomes its Owner. The player must be known to the server (has joined before).

  • Permission: doorplus.command.manage. Role: Owner.
  • Fails if the new owner already has a door with the same name.
  • When a player runs it (without doorplus.admin.bypass.limits), the new owner must have room in their door limit. For an offline recipient the limits.doors-per-player value is used. The console does not check the limit.
  • Example: /dp transfer castle_gate Alex

docs.title: /dp delete
docs.text:
/dp delete <door> [confirm]

Deletes a door. Without confirm, Door+ only asks you to confirm: Delete ... for good? Type /door delete #12 confirm to confirm. Run it again with confirm to delete.

  • Permission: doorplus.command.manage. Role: Owner.
  • Example: /dp delete #12 confirm

docs.title: Access entries
docs.text:
Access entries say who may use a door when its privacy is restricted, and who is Admin. See Privacy and roles.

All access commands need doorplus.command.manage and the Owner role on the door.

docs.title: /dp access list
docs.text:
/dp access list <door>

Lists the entries of a door with type, subject and role, and shows the door's privacy.

  • Example: /dp access list castle_gate

docs.title: /dp access add
docs.text:
/dp access add <door> <player|group|permission> <subject> [user|admin]

Adds an entry, or changes the role of an existing entry. The role is user if you leave it out. owner is not accepted.

  • player: a player name known to the server.
  • group: a LuckPerms group name. Needs doorplus.access.group and LuckPerms installed.
  • permission: a permission node; any player with that node gets the entry. Needs doorplus.access.permission.
  • The list is limited by limits.max-access-entries (see Limits).
  • Examples: /dp access add castle_gate player Alex, /dp access add castle_gate group guards admin, /dp access add castle_gate permission myserver.castle

docs.title: /dp access remove
docs.text:
/dp access remove <door> <player|group|permission> <subject>

Removes an entry. Tab completion lists the current entries of the door.

  • Example: /dp access remove castle_gate player Alex

docs.title: Triggers
docs.text:
Triggers are blocks, redstone, entities or areas that operate a door or a group. See Triggers.

All trigger commands need doorplus.command.manage. A target is a <door> or group:<group>. You need the Admin role on the door, or you must own the group (or have doorplus.admin.bypass.manage). A trigger you cannot edit answers Trigger not found.

docs.title: /dp trigger list
docs.text:
/dp trigger list <door|group:group>

Lists the triggers of a door or a group with ID, type, position, action, access mode and whether it is enabled.

  • Examples: /dp trigger list castle_gate, /dp trigger list group:castle

docs.title: /dp trigger add
docs.text:
/dp trigger add <door|group:group> <block|redstone|entity|proximity> [action] [radius]

Starts the selection mode: click the block or entity you want to link. For proximity you choose the centre instead. Type /dp cancel to stop. The selection times out after triggers.selection-timeout-seconds.

  • action (optional): toggle, open, close, follow or goto.
  • radius (optional, proximity only): 1 to limits.max-proximity-radius.
  • Extra permission: doorplus.trigger.<kind>, for example doorplus.trigger.block.
  • Players only.
  • Custom blocks, furniture and NPC triggers are linked from the menu, not with this command.
  • Examples: /dp trigger add castle_gate block, /dp trigger add castle_gate block open, /dp trigger add group:castle proximity toggle 5

docs.title: /dp trigger remove
docs.text:
/dp trigger remove <trigger id>

Removes a trigger.

  • Example: /dp trigger remove 12

docs.title: /dp trigger set
docs.text:
/dp trigger set <trigger id> <option> <value>
Option Values Applies to action toggle, open, close, follow, goto (only the actions valid for this trigger and its target) all arg stop number, from 0 only when the action is goto access inherit, public, restricted, owner-only all except redstone cooldown ticks, 0 to 72000 (20 ticks = 1 second) all cancel-vanilla true / false all except redstone and proximity enabled true / false all radius 1 to limits.max-proximity-radius proximity only exit-delay ticks, 0 to 72000 proximity only

An option that does not fit the trigger answers The option ... does not apply to this trigger.

  • Examples: /dp trigger set 12 action open, /dp trigger set 12 cooldown 40, /dp trigger set 7 radius 6

docs.title: /dp trigger access
docs.text:
/dp trigger access <trigger id> <add|remove> <player|group|permission> <subject>

Edits the trigger's own access entries (used when the trigger's access mode is restricted). Adding a group needs doorplus.access.group and LuckPerms; adding a permission needs doorplus.access.permission.

  • Example: /dp trigger access 12 add player Alex

docs.title: /dp trigger inspect
docs.text:
/dp trigger inspect

Starts the inspection mode: click a block or entity to see the triggers linked to it. Type /dp cancel to stop.

  • Players only.

docs.title: Keys
docs.text:
Keys are items that open a door. See Keys.

All key commands need doorplus.command.manage and the Admin role on the door.

Command What it does /dp key mode <door> <none\|alternative\|required> Sets how the key is used. /dp key create <door> Turns the item in your main hand into a key of the door. Players only. /dp key custom <door> Uses the custom item (ItemsAdder, Nexo, Oraxen, CraftEngine) in your hand as the key. Players only. /dp key give <door> [player] Gives a copy of the key to an online player, or to yourself if you leave the player out. The console must name a player. /dp key consume <door> <true\|false> Whether one key is used up each time the door is opened with it. /dp key reset <door> Generates a new key: all old keys stop working. /dp key remove <door> Removes the key of the door.

Examples:

/dp key create vault_door
/dp key mode vault_door required
/dp key give vault_door Alex

docs.title: Groups
docs.text:
A group operates several doors together. See Groups.

Operating a group (toggle, open, close) needs doorplus.command.toggle. Every other group action needs doorplus.command.manage. You can only use your own groups unless you have doorplus.admin.bypass.manage.

Command What it does /dp group create <name> Creates a group. Name rules as for doors. Limited by limits.max-groups-per-player. Players only. /dp group delete <group> Deletes a group. The doors are not deleted. /dp group rename <group> <name> Renames a group. /dp group add <group> <door> Adds a door. You need the Admin role on the door. Limited by limits.max-doors-per-group. /dp group remove <group> <door> Removes a door, even one on which you lost your role. /dp group list Lists your groups with ID and number of doors. In the console: every group. /dp group info <group> Shows the owner and the doors of a group. /dp group toggle\|open\|close <group> Operates every door of the group. Players go through each door's access check; the console skips it and gets a summary Group ...: x/y doors moving.

Examples:

/dp group create castle
/dp group add castle gate_left
/dp group add castle gate_right
/dp group open castle

docs.title: Administration
docs.text:
Each admin action has its own permission. All of them are children of doorplus.admin.* and default to operators.

Command Permission What it does /dp admin reload doorplus.admin.reload Reloads config.yml and the language files. Changes to storage need a restart. See Configuration. /dp admin pause doorplus.admin.pause Pauses every door movement; run it again to resume. While paused, nobody can operate doors. The pause is not saved: a restart resumes movements. /dp admin stopall doorplus.admin.stopall Finishes every running animation instantly and reports how many. /dp admin cleanup doorplus.admin.cleanup Removes orphan animation entities left in the world and reports how many. /dp admin import bigdoors [file] [--dry-run] doorplus.admin.import Imports the doors of BigDoors. Without file it reads plugins/BigDoors/doorDB.db. A relative path is looked up in the plugins folder. --dry-run only checks the file and reports, without importing. See Importing from BigDoors. /dp admin version doorplus.admin.version Shows plugin and API version, server version, storage type, animation engine, active integrations, hooks, number of doors, triggers and groups, and the licensee. /dp admin debug <door> doorplus.admin.debug Writes the internal state of a door to the server console (for bug reports). /dp admin claim <door> doorplus.admin.claim You become the Owner of the door; the previous owner loses it. Players only. A bare name is searched among every door of the server; if several doors have it, use #id.

Examples:

/dp admin import bigdoors --dry-run
/dp admin import bigdoors BigDoors/doorDB.db
/dp admin claim #12

docs.title: Console usage
docs.text:
The console always acts as Owner of every door and sees every door. Door references in the console: #id, owner:name, or a bare name that only one door on the server uses.

Works in the console Players only help, list (no argument = all doors), info menu (also /dp alone opens the help in the console) toggle, open, close, goto (access check skipped) create, cancel, redefine, tp lock, unlock, rename, set, privacy, transfer (no limit check), delete trigger add, trigger inspect access list, access add, access remove key create, key custom, key give without a player trigger list, trigger remove, trigger set, trigger access group create key mode, key give <door> <player>, key consume, key reset, key remove admin claim group delete, rename, add, remove, list, info, toggle, open, close (use #id or owner:name) admin reload, pause, stopall, cleanup, import, version, debug

A player-only command run from the console answers Only players can do this.

Command blocks and other plugins

Command blocks and plugins that run commands as the console can use the console forms, for example dp open #12. This is a simple way to open doors from other plugins' events.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: This page explains every key of plugins/DoorPlus/config.yml, section by section: type, default, allowed values, effect, and when a change takes effect. It is for server administrators.

docs.title: How the file works
docs.text:
• Door+ creates config.yml on the first start. After an update, keys that are missing from your file are added automatically with their default value and comment; your existing values are kept.
  • Do not edit config-version. Door+ uses it to track the file format.
  • Durations in ticks: 20 ticks = 1 second.
  • Values such as PRIVATE, block_display or EASE_IN_OUT are not case-sensitive.
  • Material and entity names are the Bukkit names, for example TRIPWIRE_HOOK, ARMOR_STAND.

docs.title: Invalid values
docs.text:
An invalid value never stops the server. Door+ writes a warning to the console such as Invalid value for 'limits.max-blocks-to-move': 9999; using default 64 and uses the default value instead. Your file is not changed.

  • A number outside its range, a decimal where a whole number is required, or text where a number or true/false is required counts as invalid.
  • Unknown names inside a list (materials, entity types, collision modes) are skipped one by one with a warning; the rest of the list is used. This lets one file work on several Minecraft versions.

docs.title: Reload
docs.text:
/dp admin reload re-reads config.yml and the language files. If the file cannot be read (for example a YAML syntax error), you see Reload failed: the previous configuration is still active. and the details are in the console.

Change When it takes effect storage.* Only after a server restart. Reload prints Changes to the 'storage' section require a server restart. integrations.* Only after a server restart: integrations are hooked when Door+ starts. Everything else After /dp admin reload, from the next action that uses it (next door movement, next creation, next trigger link).

docs.title: General
docs.text: Key Type Default Effect config-version number 1 Format version of the file. Do not change it. debug true/false false Writes extra diagnostic messages to the console. Turn it on only when you investigate a problem.

docs.title: language
docs.text:
Key Type Default Effect language.default text en Language file used for the console and for players when per-player does not apply. Must match a file in plugins/DoorPlus/lang/ without .yml (bundled: en, it). If no such file exists, Door+ warns and uses en. language.per-player true/false true Each player sees messages in their Minecraft client language when a matching file exists.

Details on the Language page.

docs.title: storage
docs.text:
Needs a restart. Full setup guide on the Storage page.

Key Type Default Allowed values Effect storage.type text sqlite sqlite, mysql, mariadb Database used. storage.server-id text default 1 to 32 characters Identifies this server when several servers share one database. storage.table-prefix text dp_ 1 to 16 letters, digits or _ Prefix of every table name. storage.sqlite.file text doorplus.db file name SQLite file, inside plugins/DoorPlus/. storage.mysql.host text localhost Database server address. storage.mysql.port number 3306 1 to 65535 Database server port. storage.mysql.database text doorplus Database (schema) name. storage.mysql.username text doorplus Login user. storage.mysql.password text '' Login password. storage.mysql.properties text 'useSSL=false' Extra JDBC connection options, key=value joined with &. storage.pool.max-size number 4 1 to 64 Maximum open connections (MySQL/MariaDB only; SQLite always uses 1). storage.pool.connection-timeout-ms number 10000 250 to 600000 How long to wait for a connection, in milliseconds.

docs.title: worlds
docs.text: Key Type Default Effect worlds.disabled list of world names [] Doors cannot be created in these worlds. Existing doors there keep working. Write the names exactly as the world folders, for example [world_nether, minigames].

docs.title: defaults
docs.text:
Initial settings of every new door. Changing them does not change existing doors.

Key Type Default Allowed values Effect defaults.privacy text PRIVATE PRIVATE, RESTRICTED, PUBLIC Who can use a new door. See Privacy and roles. defaults.allow-redstone true/false false Whether redstone can operate a new door. defaults.protect-blocks true/false false Whether the blocks of a new door are protected from breaking. defaults.auto-close-seconds number 0 0 to 86400 Auto-close time of a new door; 0 = off. defaults.region-access true/false false Members and owners of the WorldGuard region around the door can use it (only for RESTRICTED doors). See WorldGuard.

docs.title: limits
docs.text:
Every key of this section, with ranges, permission overrides and examples, is explained on the Limits page.

Key Default limits.doors-per-player 10 limits.max-door-blocks 500 limits.max-triggers-per-door 16 limits.max-blocks-to-move 64 limits.max-trigger-distance 64 limits.max-access-entries 64 limits.max-proximity-radius 16 limits.max-auto-close-seconds 600 limits.max-platform-stops 8 limits.max-groups-per-player 10 limits.max-doors-per-group 16 limits.speed-multiplier.min / .max 0.25 / 4.0

docs.title: creation
docs.text: Key Type Default Allowed values Effect creation.timeout-seconds number 120 20 to 3600 A door creation with no activity for this long is cancelled.

docs.title: blocks
docs.text:
Which blocks can be part of a door. All values are lists of block materials.

Key Default Effect blocks.replaceable [WATER, LAVA, SNOW, FERN, SHORT_GRASS, TALL_GRASS, SEAGRASS, TALL_SEAGRASS] Blocks a moving door may overwrite, and that do not count as door blocks when you select a region. Air is always replaceable. blocks.passable [BARRIER, LIGHT, STRUCTURE_VOID] Blocks a moving door may pass through: the door replaces them while it is there and puts them back when it leaves. Blocks with a block entity (chests, signs, ...) are refused here with a warning. A block listed here is removed from replaceable. blocks.blacklist [BEDROCK, END_PORTAL, END_PORTAL_FRAME, NETHER_PORTAL, END_GATEWAY, COMMAND_BLOCK, CHAIN_COMMAND_BLOCK, REPEATING_COMMAND_BLOCK, STRUCTURE_BLOCK, JIGSAW, REINFORCED_DEEPSLATE] Blocks that can never be part of a door. blocks.whitelist [] If not empty, only these blocks can be part of a door. blocks.allow-tile-entities false Reserved. Only false is accepted in this version: blocks with a block entity (chests, furnaces, signs, ...) cannot be part of a door. true is replaced by false with a warning.

If one of the list keys is not a list at all, the default list is used.

docs.title: animation
docs.text:
How door movements are drawn.

Key Type Default Allowed values Effect animation.engine text block_display block_display, falling_block Entities used to show the moving blocks. block_display is smooth and recommended. animation.update-interval-ticks number 2 1 to 5 How often the animation is updated. Lower is smoother but costs more. animation.easing text EASE_IN_OUT LINEAR, EASE_IN_OUT EASE_IN_OUT starts and stops gently; LINEAR moves at constant speed. animation.min-ticks number 10 1 to 1200 Shortest duration of a movement. animation.max-ticks number 600 1 to 12000, not below min-ticks Longest duration of a movement. animation.viewer-range number 64 1 to 512 If no player is within this many blocks of the door, it moves instantly without animation. animation.max-animated-blocks number 1500 1 to 1000000 Doors with more blocks move instantly without animation. animation.max-global-animated-blocks number 10000 1 to 10000000 Maximum animated blocks on the whole server at once. Movements that would exceed it happen instantly. animation.display.view-range decimal 1.0 0.01 to 64 View range multiplier of the display entities (block_display engine). animation.display.fixed-brightness true/false true Gives moving blocks a fixed brightness so they do not flicker dark while moving.

docs.title: speed
docs.text:
Base speeds. Each door can change them with its speed multiplier (/dp set <door> speed). The result is always kept between animation.min-ticks and animation.max-ticks.

Key Type Default Allowed values Effect speed.blocks-per-second decimal 2.0 0.05 to 100 Speed of sliding movements (sliding doors, portcullises, platforms, ...). speed.degrees-per-second decimal 45.0 1 to 3600 Speed of rotating movements (big doors, drawbridges, ...). speed.max-tip-speed decimal 6.0 0.1 to 200 Maximum speed, in blocks per second, of the far edge of a rotating door. Large doors rotate slower so their edge does not exceed it.

docs.title: movement
docs.text: Key Type Default Allowed values Effect movement.toggle-cooldown-ticks number 0 0 to 72000 Minimum time between two movements of the same door. movement.check-swept-volume true/false true Checks the whole path of the door, not only its end position, for obstacles before moving. movement.update-neighbors true/false true Sends block updates to neighbouring blocks when a door moves (redstone, water and similar react). movement.auto-close-unloaded true/false true When an auto-close is due and the door's chunks are not loaded: true closes it instantly; false waits until the chunks are loaded.

docs.title: collision
docs.text:
How moving doors treat players and entities. See Movement.

Key Type Default Allowed values Effect collision.default-mode text none one of allowed-modes Mode of doors set to "default". If it is not in allowed-modes, the first allowed mode is used with a warning. collision.allowed-modes list [none, shulker, push] none, shulker, push Modes players can choose. none: entities pass through; shulker (shown as Solid): the moving door is solid; push: entities are pushed away. An empty list allows all three. collision.evict-on-finish true/false true When a movement ends, entities inside the door's blocks are moved out. collision.shulker.max-per-door number 200 0 to 10000 Maximum invisible collision entities per door in shulker mode. collision.push.non-players true/false true push mode also pushes mobs and dropped items, not only players. collision.push.strength decimal 1.2 0 to 10 Push strength. collision.push.max-velocity decimal 1.5 0.05 to 10 Maximum speed of a pushed entity.
